verdict.rationale: React's own docs clearly cover the modular half of the story: encapsulated components that manage their own state and compose into screens, pages and apps. Data is passed into components from outside, but nothing in the evidence describes a dependency-injection mechanism (such as context or providers), so the DI half is unproven. Missing for 10: documented dependency-injection mechanism, evidence of injecting services or dependencies into components, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can organize my app into modular, dependency-injected building blocks

citations.quote: Build encapsulated components that manage their own state, then compose them to make complex UIs.
Create your own React components like `Thumbnail`, `LikeButton`, and `Video`. Then combine them into entire screens, pages, and apps.
React apps are made out of *components*. A component is a piece of the UI (user interface) that has its own logic and appearance.
React components receive data and return what should appear on the screen.
